transcript: The Public, along with Ma-Yi Theater Company and La Jolla Playhouse is presenting a unique new play about sumo wrestling, aptly called SUMO. This is something I previously knew almost nothing about, so I obviously wouldn't consider myself very invested in it. But a great play can illuminate the humanity and the stakes present in any situation, even those that are seemingly distant from its audience. SUMO checks those boxes with flying colors. The main plotline follows a junior wrestler named Akio who's learning the ropes and trying to climb the ranks among the other wrestlers. Through this lens, we the audience get completely immersed in the training facility, the internal politics and rituals of the whole system, and the mindset and determination of these wrestlers. You really get a sense of how sumo isn't just a sport for these guys, it's their entire lives, so the stakes are extremely high. And other than the novelty of the subject matter and the action-packed wrestling sequences, I think there's a great story here, great acting and directing, and I loved the projection designs and the live percussion which underscores the wrestling and brings the tension to new heights. SUMO is running at The Public through the end of March. With that another playbill for my collection.
